data.name: Nishithi
data.gender_notes: Nishithi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nishithi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'nisha', meaning 'night', and 'stha', indicating 'end' or 'standing'. It refers to the end of night or dawn, symbolizing hope and new beginnings. The name Nishithi carries the meaning “Night's End” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nishithi usually hope their child will grow to embody night's end and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of hope and renewal, Nishithi embodies the essence of spiritual awakening as the night fades into a new day.
data.etymology: Nishithi belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night's End.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nishithi total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Nishithi is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a sage who performed severe penance to gain the boon of a son, who would become a great warrior and king. This son was Bhishma, who is one of the main characters in the epic.
Nishithi is also the name of a Jain monk and scholar who lived in the 12th century CE. He was a prominent figure in the Digambara sect and is known for his works on Jain philosophy and scripture.
